Simulate power for a design

Source: R/simulate.R
simulate_power.Rd

Runs an on-demand simulation for a single design cell: generate networks and data under the grid's data-generating family, fit the method, and score its FDR-controlled differential calls. Use this directly to answer designs the grid does not cover (other p, unequal group sizes, other FDR targets), or via power_for(..., simulate = TRUE).

Usage

simulate_power(
  p,
  n,
  method,
  perturbation = "structural",
  fdr = 0.05,
  reps = 20L,
  n_perm = 30L,
  cores = 1L,
  seed = 1L,
  max_minutes = 60,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

p

Number of features.

n

Per-group sample size; a single number, or c(n1, n2) for unequal groups.

method

Estimation method label. See howbig_coverage() for the available methods.

perturbation

Type of differential signal: "structural" (edges appear/disappear), "magnitude" (edge weights change), or "both".

fdr

Target false-discovery rate for the differential calls.

reps

Number of simulated replicates (fresh network + data each).

n_perm

Number of label permutations for the null (ignored for multiGGM).

cores

Parallel worker processes. Workers are fresh R sessions (PSOCK), not forks, so they are safe with multithreaded BLAS such as Apple Accelerate; howbig must be installed for cores > 1.

seed

Base seed; results are reproducible for a given seed regardless of cores.

max_minutes

Refuse to start if the estimated runtime exceeds this many minutes. The estimate comes from per-fit timings of the production grid runs; raise this to run long designs deliberately.

verbose

Print progress messages.

Value

A howbig_power object with provenance = "simulated".

Details

Inference matches how the grid was scored. Frequentist methods are called against a pooled label-permutation null (one representative network, n_perm permutations with fresh data, Benjamini-Hochberg); multiGGM uses its posterior probabilities directly (direct-posterior FDR).

Simulation is slow: each replicate and each permutation is a full method fit. Start with small reps / n_perm to gauge runtime.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
simulate_power(p = 100, n = 500, method = "JGL_BIC", reps = 10)
} # }
